hub: S. A. Andrée's Arctic balloon expedition of 1897

outgoing.name: Airship
outgoing.excerpt: Andrée claimed that, with the drag rope/sails steering, his Svea had essentially become a dirigible, but this notion is rejected by modern balloonists.

outgoing.name: Climate
outgoing.excerpt: Even Ekholm, an Arctic climate researcher, had no objection to Andrée's theory of where the wind was likely to take them.

outgoing.name: Finland
outgoing.excerpt: On one occasion he was blown clear across the Baltic to Finland.

outgoing.name: French language
outgoing.excerpt: The balloon, originally called Le Pôle Nord (French for "The North Pole"), was to be renamed Örnen ( Swedish for "The Eagle").

outgoing.name: Norway
outgoing.excerpt: Further discoveries were made by the M/K Isbjørn of Tromsø, Norway, a sealing sloop chartered by news reporters to waylay the Bratvaag.

outgoing.name: Scurvy
outgoing.excerpt: There was also lemon juice, though not as much of this precaution against scurvy as other polar explorers usually thought necessary.

outgoing.name: Walrus
outgoing.excerpt: Seals, walruses, and especially polar bears were shot and eaten throughout the march.
